hue: Waxy translucent yellowish-green outer tepals with shorter dark reddish-purple inner tepals
visual: Large, much-branched deciduous shrub grown chiefly for its intensely fragrant winter flowers. Small waxy, almost translucent yellow flowers appear directly along bare previous-season stems before the foliage emerges.
water: Water regularly while establishing. Mature plants prefer consistent moisture but are reasonably tolerant of short dry periods once established.
aspect: Full sun in a warm, sheltered position, ideally against a south- or east-facing wall.
soil: Moist but well-drained or freely drained fertile soil; tolerant of chalk, clay, loam and sand and a wide range of soil pH.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged ground and very exposed sites. Shelter and summer warmth help wood ripen and promote reliable flowering.
prune: Requires little routine pruning. Immediately after flowering, remove dead, damaged or badly placed shoots and lightly shape established plants if necessary.
cvs: Species form. Notable selections include 'Luteus' and 'Grandiflorus', but the supplied plant is Chimonanthus praecox without a named cultivar.
hardinessNote: Hardy in most parts of the UK, tolerating approximately -15 to -10°C when established, though a sheltered position is recommended.
resilience: Generally pest-free and reliably hardy in sheltered UK gardens. Rarely susceptible to honey fungus. Established plants are long-lived but perform best where protected from cold winds.
uses: Winter gardens, scented gardens, shrub borders, cottage gardens, courtyards and wall-side planting near paths or entrances where its winter fragrance can be appreciated.
foliage: Deciduous, lance-shaped to ovate dark green leaves approximately 5–12 cm long, emerging after the winter flowers.
container: Possible while young but not ideal as a permanent container shrub because mature plants become large and flower best when well established in the ground.
uncertain: Mature size varies with climate and training. RHS gives approximately 2.5–4 m tall and 1.5–2.5 m wide, while Kew describes typical cultivated plants around 3 m high and wide.
Flowering performance can vary considerably with site; plants in warm, sunny, sheltered positions generally flower more reliably.
